Scope: product `trips`, the same 52 published documents (corpus hash
`ba68007733e42ce82ee8e416b3360d3a3084647b6fd74440bc699660a6fb50c2`), against
`tasks/trip_booking_and_settlement_desk/trips.extended.yaml` and the task-tool contracts. Entry conditions as
cited in `policy_kb/trip_booking_and_settlement_desk/0.md`: policy-side PASS at round 3, `check_docs.py` and
`check_traceability.py` both green (`task 1.json copied 16 missing 0 ok True`), runtime-visible view and
tool-shaped DB path supplied. Nothing missing from the input.

The 13 base policies, the 10 facet documents and the retired surface are audited once, in
`policy_kb/trip_booking_and_settlement_desk/0.md` §A and §C, and are not re-audited here; findings **B-1**,
**B-2** and **B-3** recorded there stand for this task too. This file audits the two extended policies this
task's tree runs through — `trips_ext_young_driver_surcharge` and `trips_ext_extension_quote` — and its one
prerequisite, and records the additional finding **B-4**.

## kb_to_source

Traced sentence by sentence as in task 0's file. Additions found beyond **B-1**, **B-2** and **B-3**:

- **B-4 (bijection-critical, outcome-bearing).** `extension_young_driver_share_basis_bf64bc7b`, closing
  sentence of "### Reading the ladder": "The surcharge is spread over the days of the reserved period, which
  run from the first day of that period to the last, both days counted; **the daily share is taken to the
  nearest cent.**" The source's `young_driver_share_basis` ladder says only "the young-driver share is that
  surcharge spread evenly over the days of the reserved period and taken for each extended day", and its
  `compute` rounds **once, at the end**:
  `yd_share = RND(surcharge_line / reserved_days_b * extended_days, 2)`. The KB has inserted an intermediate
  rounding the source does not carry. On this task's figures — surcharge 108.42 over 14 reserved days across
  2 extended days — the source gives `RND(108.42 / 14 x 2, 2) = 15.49` and the KB gives 7.74 x 2 = 15.48, so
  the quote comes out at 192.52 against the scored 192.53. (The first half of the same sentence, "which run
  from the first day of that period to the last, both days counted", **is** faithful: it renders the
  source's `reserved_days_b = DAYS(trip_start, trip_end) + 1`.) Note that the document's own worked
  hypothetical — 180.00 over 20 days — divides exactly, so it does not expose the divergence.

No other additions in the eleven documents of these two policies. Nothing asks for a confirmation, a second
review, a notification or a fallback procedure the source does not carry.

**Prerequisite-side specific checks:**
- *Cross-problem operational guidance*: **none**. No document of `trips_ext_extension_quote` names
  `post_young_driver_surcharge_8e3312c3`, names the young-driver policy, or tells the reader what to do if
  the surcharge is not yet standing. No document of `trips_ext_young_driver_surcharge` names
  `submit_extension_request_8f69bfd6` or the quote.
- *A task's opening world state written in as a policy fact*: **none**. No document states that a
  reservation carries an expired request, that an election carries 728.00 of fees, that a deposit line
  stands, or that any customer is under the young-driver threshold. Every hypothetical uses figures unlike
  this task's world (21 reserved days, 1150.00/640.00 of fees, 2000 granted miles, 30 days with 3 drivers,
  the 1st-to-20th reserved period, 22 days and 40 hours, 1250.00/410.00 of fees, 20 days and 180.00).

## policy_side_notes

- **P-1** (prose/compute divergence on the fee limb), **P-2** (a residue that restates its own withdrawn
  fragment) and **P-3** (unstated day-counting conventions) are recorded in
  `policy_kb/trip_booking_and_settlement_desk/0.md`. P-1 is the root of **B-4**'s sibling finding **B-1** and
  bites hardest here: the source's factor prose gives the renderer no words for the restriction that decides
  the tier, and the GT's own `factor_trace` has to supply them ("the daily protection fees charged on it come
  to 728.00 … The 109.20 young-driver protection surcharge raised on the same election is not a daily
  protection fee and is excluded by the rule").
- **P-5 — the source ladder gives no rounding for `yd_share`.** The method text says only "spread evenly …
  and taken for each extended day"; the rounding that decides the cent lives only in `compute`
  (`RND(surcharge_line / reserved_days_b * extended_days, 2)`). The renderer had to invent something, and
  invented the wrong thing (**B-4**). The fault recorded against the KB stands — the documents may not close
  what the source leaves open — but the policy side left it open.
- **P-6 — a base clause in tension with the extended policy.** `trips_evt_extension` states "The extension is
  priced only where the host's decision is recorded no later than the decision window counted forward from
  the scheduled return of the reservation", and no `overwrite` retires it, while
  `trips_ext_extension_quote` prices the extra time **before** the request reaches the register and before
  any host decision exists. The KB renders both sides exactly as the source leaves them
  (`extension_requests_and_extended_time_pricing_1ad7935c` "**Decision window.**" against
  `extension_quote_desk_note_fa4311e0`'s opening), so this is a policy-side tension, not a rendering defect.
  It is resolvable in practice — the base clause governs whether an extension is *applied and priced onto the
  reservation*, the extended policy governs the quote carried on the register entry — but the source does not
  say so.
- **P-4** (`verify_member_identity` scored with no home in this charter) applies to this task too.

## source_to_kb (revision 2)

### B-1 — CLOSED

The charter now states the restriction in **prose**, in both of this task's policies, not only in `compute`:

> `trips_ext_young_driver_surcharge.rule` — "…and the **daily** protection fees charged on it come to at
> least eight hundred dollars, **however many lines they stand as and whenever they were raised**, the
> protection adjustment is four percentage points off…"
> `trips_ext_extension_quote.rule` — "Where the trip's protection election stands active and the **daily**
> protection fees charged on it come to at least eight hundred dollars, however many lines they stand as and
> whenever they were raised, the cover credit is fourteen dollars for each extended day…"

and both rules carry the exclusion sentence:

> "The fees counted are the daily protection fee lines raised on that election and those alone; a line
> raised on it for anything else — **a young-driver protection surcharge**, a level-change difference, an
> additional-driver fee, a deductible or a credit — is not a daily protection fee and is not counted."

`young_driver_protection_adjustment_94952a2c` and `extension_protection_cover_credit_b9c9275c` each carry
both **verbatim**, under a section headed "Which fees are counted", and each adds a worked case on the exact
failure mode (an additional-driver fee of 300.00 that does not lift a 640.00 election over the floor; a
deductible of 500.00 that does not lift a 410.00 one). The exclusion names, by its own `charge_basis`, the
109.20 `young_driver_protection_surcharge` row that broke round 1. The positive limb — "counted however many
lines they stand as and whenever they were raised" — forecloses the opposite error of reading only the
latest or the largest line. `inputs.history` and `compute` still filter `charge_basis='daily_protection_fee'`;
prose and compute now agree. `grep -i "daily protection fee"` matches all three fee documents; the bare
phrase "the protection fees charged on it" occurs nowhere in the corpus.

### B-4 — CLOSED

The charter's `young_driver_share_basis` ladder now carries the rounding, where at round 1 it carried none:

> "…spread evenly over the days of the reserved period — which run from the first day of that period to the
> last, both days counted — and taken for each extended day, **the share being brought to the nearest cent
> once the spreading and the taking have both been done and at no earlier step**"

`extension_young_driver_share_basis_bf64bc7b` carries that clause in **both** tiers, and adds a section
"Where the cent falls" whose worked example is built to expose the difference — 145.00 over a 13-day reserved
period, "The spreading gives 11.153846… USD for each day … 145.00 divided by 13 and taken for 2 extended days
is 22.307692… USD, which comes to **22.31 USD**" — carrying the unrounded daily figure through the taking in
plain sight. This matches `compute`'s `RND(surcharge_line / reserved_days_b * extended_days, 2)` exactly.
`grep -c "daily share"` → **0 corpus-wide**. The document also gained the negative restriction on which
surcharge lines are summed ("every young-driver surcharge line standing on the reservation taken together,
as each was raised and whatever was afterwards done about it"), sourced verbatim from the ladder.

## What changed that this task reads

Two of the three changed documents are read by this task's derivations, and in both the change is confined
to a sentence no derivation uses:

| Document | Edit | What this task takes from it, and its status |
|---|---|---|
| `reservation_pricing_and_line_composition_156172b6` | the unsourced N-2 sentence "The plan's published young-driver percentage and its young-driver threshold remain the plan's figures and are unaffected." **deleted** | The **priced-line state gate** ("a line is posted only while the reservation is in the requested, booked or in-progress state") and the **young-driver residue** ("Where the driver is under the young-driver threshold on the first day of the reserved period, the young-driver surcharge is posted as its own line, so that it can be reversed on its own if the driver's age is later corrected") — both **present and untouched**. The B-3 repair judged at revision 2 is intact. |
| `extension_requests_and_extended_time_pricing_1ad7935c` | meta-phrase "What stands from that sentence is the rest of it:" **deleted**; the residue **re-seated** ahead of the withdrawal note | The **lead time**, the **maximum additional hours**, "A request standing on the extension request register is not a change to the reservation" and "A declined or expired request leaves the reservation untouched" — all four **present and untouched**. The last is what keeps the expired 48-hour request from counting against the 72-hour maximum. |

Neither document supplies a tier, a constant, a ladder or a rounding position for this task. The six
documents that decide `surcharge_amount` and the six that decide `quoted_amount` are all outside the changed
set, as are both hubs.

**The N-2 deletion here removes a real hazard for this task specifically.** The deleted sentence declared
the plan's published young-driver percentage "unaffected". On the Keyturn Weekly Rate Plan that figure is 15
per cent, coinciding with the policy's own `rate_standard`, so it could not have shown here — but it is the
plan column a reader is invited to apply instead of the ladder, and on any other plan it diverges. Its
removal closes that invitation.

## The re-seating, verified against the charter

Checked by arithmetic rather than by reading, because it is the one edit that is not a pure deletion. The
charter's residue for `trips_evt_extension` — the base sentence minus `overwrite.superseded_clause` — is
"the original period keeps its original price, and no discount for length is recalculated on the extended
reservation", and the document's re-seated clause, normalised, is **character-for-character identical**.
Nothing added, nothing dropped. It was also necessary: here the residue was carried *only* inside the
deleted meta-statement, so deletion alone would have dropped a clause in force.
